# OMG (Oh My GitHub) agent instructions

Do not implement, suggest, report, or propose security issues unless the user explicitly asks for a security review.
Inspect the OpenCode implementation at `/Users/igor/Documents/ChatGPT/opencode` and [anomalyco/opencode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) for related requests.

## Wiki index

- [OpenCode workflow](wiki/opencode.md)
- [Test OpenCode execution](wiki/opencode-v2-experiment.md)
- [Oh My Github App](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/oh-my-github-app.md)
- [Temporary Mac SSH access](wiki/access.md)
- [Testing and verification](wiki/testing.md)
- [OmGithub publishing](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/omgithub.md)


## Main project file

The main project file is [.github/workflows/opencode.yml](.github/workflows/opencode.yml).

Keep the local [game issue E2E skill](.agents/skills/game-issue-e2e/SKILL.md)
aligned with this workflow. Create an issue with `OpenCode` and only user-requested mode labels already attached, to start the native `issues.opened` listener. Wait only for the
initial OpenCode session link during E2E kickoff. Install the listener on the
default branch before requesting execution. Validate author access and freeze
the request inside Actions before starting the reusable execution job.
Set repository variable `OPENCODE_ACCESS=everyone` to accept any issue author
for labeled issues. Keep the App as a setup
helper. Use Actions concurrency to serialize each issue.
Store `branch` in an `omgithub-request:v1` JSON HTML comment to select the
project checkout, result base, and workflow. Let default-branch preparation
dispatch the selected branch. Run preparation and OpenCode in that branch run.

## Shell timing

When writing shell scripts,
always add explicit per-command execution-time measurements between commands.
Use `/usr/bin/time -p` or a small timing helper around each meaningful command;
the outer command duration is not sufficient because it hides which step is
slow or hung. Use `/usr/bin/time` only in scripts; do not invoke it directly in
interactive shell commands.

## Ideas

Store durable implementation ideas as individual Markdown files under
`./ideas/`, using descriptive kebab-case filenames such as
`ideas/opencode-oauth-env-auth.md`.




## Links in handoffs

When a relevant URL or stable identifier exists, include a clickable Markdown
link in the user-facing response. Link GitHub issues, Actions runs, pull
requests, commits, releases, public app URLs, and Codex tasks/threads rather
than reporting only their numbers or plain text. For Codex tasks/threads, use
the `codex://threads/<thread-id>` URL format.

When mentioning a commit, append its relative age in hours or days.

## OpenCode GitHub Actions

To execute an issue, create it with `OpenCode` and only mode labels explicitly requested by the user.
Check for a native `issues` run and successful preparation.
The workflow starts a temporary AgentsWeb SSH session,
verifies it, runs OpenCode, and cleans up the SSH session afterward.

When monitoring a triggered run, use `gh run watch <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --exit-status` for overall job status.
Do not use `gh run view --log` to read logs from a running task: GitHub reports that
logs are unavailable until completion. Use `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>`
for the live Actions log over SSH. Do not use tight `for` loops around `gh run list`,
which needlessly consume GitHub API rate limit.

Free OpenCode models are limited per egress IP, not per account.
Treat a local `FreeUsageLimitError` 429 as local only.
Read the runner's own `Selected model` and provider errors before blaming quota.
Use `retryAfterMs` as the reset bound.
Run repeated V2 tests with a connected provider; do not spend the free allowance on retries.

Interrupting a V2 turn before the assistant message projects leaves no stopped message to save.
Wait for that assistant message before requiring the interrupted idle marker.

To connect to an issue's live worker, find its run ID with
`gh run list --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --workflow opencode.yml --status in_progress`,
then run `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>` to discover the host and port and SSH
with `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb` as shown by the helper.

When the user asks to check a live OpenCode workflow, always pull the runner logs
over SSH first, using `scripts/ssh-run-log.sh` or a targeted SSH read from the
same runner. Base the answer on those logs before discussing whether an action
is confirmed; do not lead with a generic inability-to-confirm statement when
live log evidence can be collected.

For real-time inspection from a live temporary SSH session, use the helper:

```sh
bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>
```

The helper discovers the temporary SSH command from the triggering issue or pull
request, then follows the freshest `_diag/pages` log. The runner uploads chunks from
`_diag/blocks` to GitHub. Do not print environment files, tokens, or private keys while
inspecting the runner.

## Mac SSH access

The Mac private key stays at `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`. Its public key is
stored in the repository Actions secret `AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY`. The issue
commented by the workflow contains a directly usable command such as:

```sh
ssh -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
```

The command works only while the corresponding Actions job is running.

## Connecting to a live OpenCode worker

Use the repository helper to discover the worker host and port from the broker
or issue comment. It uses the persistent local key `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`:

```sh
bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub
```

For an interactive shell, reuse the host and port printed by the helper and
use the same key:

```sh
ssh -tt -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no \
  -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null \
  -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb \
  -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
```

Do not substitute the generated runner key under `sshworker/outputs/keys/`; it
can produce a misleading `Permission denied (publickey)` result. Temporary
worker SSH access ends when the Actions job and session are cleaned up. Never
print secrets while inspecting a worker.

# 🤯 OMG — Oh My GitHub ### 🚀 One Prompt In. A Full Game or App Out. 🚀 [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-🔥%20works-brightgreen?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/denaidark/OhMyGithub?style=for-the-badge&logo=github)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/issues) [![GitHub Actions](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub%20Actions-automated-2088FF?style=for-the-badge&logo=githubactions&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![OpenCode](https://img.shields.io/badge/powered%20by-OpenCode-111111?style=for-the-badge)](https://opencode.ai/) ```text ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗ ║ DESCRIBE IT → BUILD IT → TEST IT → PLAY IT ║ ║ ║ ║ One GitHub issue. One prompt. A complete project. ║ ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝ ``` **No API keys to configure. No server to maintain. No local setup maze.**
--- ## 🤯 What Is OMG? > **Your GitHub issue becomes the product brief.** OMG (Oh My GitHub) is an automated GitHub Actions workflow for creating complete browser games and app projects from one natural-language prompt. Write what you want in an issue and add the `OpenCode` label. OpenCode checks out the project, uses the shared skills, builds the experience, runs tests, verifies the result, and publishes an immutable OmGithub project link from the finished commit. Yes, it creates the code. Yes, it runs the verification loop. Yes, it can expose the result in a temporary browser URL. ## 🧠 TL;DR 1. Open a GitHub issue. 2. Describe the game or app you want. 3. Add the `OpenCode` label to the issue. 4. Let GitHub Actions build, test, verify, and propose the result. ```text Your idea → GitHub issue → OpenCode → tests → immutable OmGithub project ``` ## ⚡ Quick Start Create an issue in your repository with a concrete request: ```text Build a neon asteroid game. Requirements: - Arrow-key movement - Score and restart button - Win and lose states - Responsive browser layout - Run tests and verify it in a browser ``` That is the whole user-facing workflow. GitHub Actions handles the runner, OpenCode handles implementation, and the workflow handles verification plus the immutable project commit. To run against an existing non-default branch, end the issue title with a `branch: ` directive. The directive selects the checkout and is removed before the issue body is sent to OpenCode: ```sh gh issue create \ --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub \ --title "Custom branch smoke test branch: codex/omgithub-site" \ --body "Build a tiny browser page." \ --label Goal \ --label OpenCode ``` The GitHub App validates the branch before dispatching. If the directive is absent, the repository default branch remains the target. ## 🌍 What Can You Build? | 🎯 Use case | ✨ Example | |---|---| | 🎮 Arcade games | Breakout, Space Invaders, Asteroids, Match-3 | | 🧩 Puzzle games | Word games, logic puzzles, card games | | 🏃 Interactive demos | Physics experiments, simulations, visual toys | | 📊 Dashboards | Filters, charts, status panels, analytics views | | 🛠️ Internal tools | Trackers, generators, small workflow apps | | 🌐 Landing pages | Product pages, portfolios, interactive showcases | | 🧪 Prototypes | Turn a product idea into a runnable proof of concept | | 📱 Browser apps | Responsive tools that work on desktop and mobile | ## 🧰 What Happens Automatically? > **The workflow is the product.** - 📥 Checks out your repository and the shared OpenCode skills. - 🏷️ Synchronizes `model/*` and `skill/*` labels. - 🧭 Reads issue labels to select the model and requested skills. - 🤖 Runs OpenCode against the current project. - 🧪 Runs a second verification prompt after implementation. - 🌐 Starts the app and checks the local runtime. - 🔗 Creates a temporary public preview URL when verification passes. - 🔀 Creates and pushes an `opencode/` branch. - 🕹️ Adds an `Open Project` link backed by the repository path, with full-commit links retained for compatibility. - 💬 Posts progress and access details back to the issue. - 🧹 Cleans up temporary tunnels and runner processes. ## 🏷️ Model and Skill Labels Labels let you control the workflow without editing YAML. ```text model/opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free skill/load-sketchfab-threejs skill/gauntlet-loop ``` The workflow validates the selected labels, passes them into OpenCode, and records the resolved model and skills in the run logs. Shared skills are discovered from: ```text .agents/skills//SKILL.md ``` ## 🔄 OpenCode Workflow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Trigger] --> B[Prepare project] B --> C[Run build.md] C --> D[Run verify.md] D --> E{Public app works?} E -- No --> F[Run public-app-fix.md] F --> E E -- Yes --> G[Run completion-report.md] G --> H{Screenshots exist?} H -- No --> I[Run screenshot-evidence.md] I --> H H -- Yes --> J[Commit and push] J --> K[Create immutable project link] K --> L[Publish report] L --> M[Complete] ``` ## 🏗️ Architecture ```text ┌──────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ │ GitHub issue │ ──▶ │ GitHub Actions │ ──▶ │ OpenCode │ │ + issue text │ │ runner + labels │ │ + .agents │ └──────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ └──────┬───────┘ │ ┌─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┐ ▼ ▼ ▼ Build code Run tests Verify app │ │ │ └─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┘ ▼ ┌────────────────────────┐ │ Commit store + preview │ └────────────────────────┘ ``` ## 🔐 Security and Access - 🔑 You do not need to create or store a project-specific AI API key. - 🖥️ You do not need to operate a dedicated build server. - ☁️ Execution happens in GitHub Actions. - 🔒 Temporary SSH and preview access exists only for the workflow run. - 👀 Review the generated commit before integrating it. - 🛡️ Restrict who can apply the `OpenCode` label in repositories that accept public issues. > “No servers needed” means no servers for you to provision or maintain. The workflow still uses GitHub-hosted Actions infrastructure and temporary workflow services. ## 📁 Project Structure ```text 📦 OMG ├─ .github/workflows/opencode.yml # 🤖 Main issue-to-project workflow ├─ wiki/opencode.md # 📖 Workflow and session notes ├─ wiki/testing.md # 🧪 Verification guidance └─ AGENTS.md # 🧭 Repository instructions ``` ## 🧪 Local Validation Validate the workflow definition before pushing changes: ```sh actionlint .github/workflows/opencode.yml git diff --check ``` ## 🐛 Troubleshooting | Problem | What to check | |---|---| | The workflow did not start | Confirm the `OpenCode` label is applied to the issue. | | A skill was not selected | Add a matching `skill/` label. | | The app URL is missing | Check the local app verification step and runner log. | | The PR was not created | Confirm OpenCode produced a diff and the workflow reached the PR step. | | The workflow ran unexpectedly | Tighten the trigger condition and trusted-user policy. | ## 🤝 Contributing Ideas, skills, game templates, verification improvements, and workflow fixes are welcome. 1. Open an issue describing the improvement. 2. Add the `OpenCode` label when you want the workflow to prototype it. 3. Review the generated commit and Open Project page carefully. 4. Add tests and runtime proof for workflow changes. ## ⭐ The Pitch The old workflow was: idea → tickets → scaffolding → setup → implementation → debugging → deployment. The OMG workflow is: **idea → issue → playable project.** If you believe software should start with a sentence instead of a sprint plan, [⭐ star the repository](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub) and try it.

playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)

Now core utilities and textures.

Let's plan coordinates and data structures.

World size: 52x52, tile size 1. Map coords: world x = (tx - SIZE/2 + 0.5), z = (tz - SIZE/2 + 0.5). Camera looks at center.

Terrain:
- `heightAt(tx,tz)`:
  - d = distance from center (26,26) normalized.
  - central flat radius 15 (tiles) => h=0.
  - rim: t = smoothstep(17, 25, r) => h = t^1.4 * 4 + noise.
  - pond at (14, 36)? Need to position. Let's set pond center tile (36, 35) radius 4.5, water level -0.3, depression. Base center (24,24). Pond southeast maybe. Another small pond? Keep one.
  - Also a low hill north-west with rocks.
  - Ground tile types: grass, dirt (around camp), sand near pond, rock (outer).
  - Buildable flat: r < 16.5 and not water and no slope.
  - Use noise for color/height subtle outside flat.
- Border cliffs: raised outside r>20 with rock. Camera limited so border visible in backdrop.

Rather than a strict flat center, subtle undulation 0.0-0.08. Buildings levels. Keep flat 0 for building area so meshes sit at y=0. For props, y=height.

Ground PlaneGeometry: width SIZE, segments 128? Vertex colors. Use `PlaneGeometry(SIZE, SIZE, 96,96)`, rotate -PI/2. Set y from height. Compute normals. Color per vertex based on terrain type and noise. Texture map grass; repeat 24. Vertex colors multiply texture. But one texture for entire ground with water depression. Vertex colors add variation. Good.

Texture grass: generate 256x256 with base #5d7a3d, speckles + blades lines. Tiling may show but texture repeat 24 with mipmaps okay. Use anisotropy 4.

Add dirt path patches around camp as separate CircleGeometry decals slightly above ground (0.02) with transparent? Use a canvas radial texture (dirt) on planes. Place 3-4 dirt patches around camp, rotate flat. Good.

Water pond mesh: CircleGeometry radius 4.6, 48 segments at y = water level (-0.18), shader; or geometry clipped to pond. Shader with time, ripples, gradient; transparent? Use depthWrite true, opaque-ish. Add foam ring? Create ring mesh with white transparent texture near shore. Later.

Rocks: InstancedMesh of dodecahedron low poly, 60 rocks around rim + some boulders near center; each has instance color gray variations. Materials MeshStandard flatShading with vertex color. Add moss? Use two instanced meshes (rock, moss?) skip.

Trees: three instanced components: trunk cylinder, foliage cone/sphere. We need 2 tree types: pine (cone layers) and broadleaf (spheres). Use InstancedMesh for trunks (all trees), pine foliage instanced (cone), broadleaf foliage instanced (icosahedron). Each tree may have 2-3 foliage clusters; use instance slots. To remove a tree, hide all its foliage/trunk instances.
- Need per-instance sway shader. Three's InstancedMesh + custom onBeforeCompile: inject into vertex shader:
```
uniform float uTime;
// instanceMatrix available
vec3 iPos = vec3(instanceMatrix[3][0], instanceMatrix[3][1], instanceMatrix[3][2]);
float sway = sin(uTime*1.2 + iPos.x*0.7 + iPos.z*0.5) * 0.03 * position.y;
transformed.x += sway;
```
For foliage position.y local, scale. Good. Same for crops maybe.
- Tree shadows: castShadow true; 60 trees okay.
- Grass tufts: InstancedMesh of crossed planes or low-poly blades. Use simple geometry with 3 thin triangles; 2000 instances, no shadow. Sway shader. Color variation via instanceColor.
- Flowers: 200 instanced small quads/spheres with colors, no shadow.
- Bushes: 30 instances of icosahedron; no shadows? cast shadow true maybe.
- Reeds around pond.

Sky:
- Dome sphere radius 400 with ShaderMaterial BackSide, uniforms topColor, horizonColor, sunColor, sunDirection, nightFactor, time. Gradient + sun glow + stars? Add separate star points.
- Fog color matched horizon. Scene.fog = FogExp2(color, 0.012) maybe. But with yaw/zoom, fog gives depth.
- Cloud sprites maybe; can do Points as soft white blobs in sky? Let's use a handful of cloud billboards made from generated soft cloud texture on planes above horizon, slowly drift and fade. Maybe too much; skip initially, add birds.
- Birds: 8 simple instanced wing shapes flapping, circling. Custom mesh 2 triangles. Good.

Lighting:
- Sun DirectionalLight with color/intensity/elevation. Direction from time of day. Shadows: camera bounds around base 30, mapSize 2048/1024. Add secondary ambient.
- At night sun replaced by moon: intensity 0.15-0.3, color blue. Hemisphere intensity 0.15.
- Fires add point lights: campfire + torches. Limit 3 dynamic lights near camera. Shadows off point lights.
- Add warm fill light? A subtle directional from opposite at 0.15 no shadows to lift shadows.

`world.trees` array {id, tx, tz, type, hp, designated, removed, instances:[{mesh,index}], scale, x,z}
`world.rocks` similar {size, designated, removed, hp, mesh,index}
`world.bushes`, `world.flowers` decorative.
`occupancy` typed array 52*52: 0 free, 1 blocked static prop/water, 2 building.
- `isBuildable(tx,tz)` checks terrain flat and free and no prop.
- Trees/rocks store blocking.
- `isWalkable(tx,tz)` false if water, cliffs, props, buildings solid. Farm/floor walkable. Door walkable.
- Keep base area flat.

Pathfinding: A*.
- Map 52x52. Use arrays. Neighbors 8-dir. Diagonal blocked if either orthogonal blocked. Cost diagonal 1.414.
- Path smoothing: from point, try farthest visible via Bresenham line where all cells walkable; pick farthest. Ensure not cutting corners.
- If target unwalkable (e.g., tree tile), find adjacent walkable nearest.
- Colonists move to work spot adjacent.

- Build a high-quality, mobile-first, Rimworld-like colony simulation game with detailed 3D graphics, animations, movement, and touch controls.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a high-quality, mobile-first, Rimworld-like colony simulation game with detailed 3D graphics, animations, movement, and touch controls.
- Built from scratch in the existing repo as a browser game using Three.js and Vite.

## Requirements
- High-detail, great-looking graphics; good animations; good movement; good controls.
- Rimworld-like gameplay.
- Must work well on mobile (touch gestures, mobile-first HUD, responsive layout).
- User provided no additional constraints or explicit scope boundaries.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js (r187) with Vite, procedural/low-poly art style rather than external assets.
- Build an isometric 3D colony sim titled “Ridgewood” with 3 starting settlers, needs, jobs, building, farming, mining, woodcutting, hauling, day/night, weather, sound, and objectives.
- Implement touch controls: one-finger pan, pinch zoom, two-finger twist rotate and pinch-pan, tap select/place, build ghost placement.
- Use postprocessing bloom, shadows, ACES tone mapping, procedural textures, instanced foliage, shader water/sky/stars, particles, and procedural WebAudio ambience.
- Warm morning opening at Day 1, ~07:20.
- Procedural low-poly characters/buildings and glassmorphism HUD.

## Work State

### Completed
- Project scaffold, dependencies, Vite build, dev server (`tmux` session `ridgewood`, port 3002).
- Core modules implemented: `utils.js`, `textures.js`, `materials.js`, `world.js`, `pathfinding.js`, `particles.js`, `buildings.js`, `entities.js`, `colony.js`, `input.js`, `ui.js`, `audio.js`, `main.js`.
- Game now renders successfully with no console/page errors.
- Fixed runtime blockers:
  - `World.applyWind`: only pushes real materials; guards undefined.
  - Added `Colony.giveJoy(c, amount)`.
  - Fixed `Colony.refreshAlerts` to call `ui.refreshAlerts()`.
  - Fixed `mergeGeometries` by converting crop cone geometry to non-indexed.
  - `groundHeight()` now bilinear-interpolates fractional coordinates, fixing beds floating at y≈3.3/5.0.
  - `WorldLabel` activity now shows real tasks instead of “On the way”; added label overlap offset.
  - Fixed placement mode not propagating to `InputController.placementType`; blueprint placement and ghost tracking now work.
  - Fixed chopped trees/mined rocks deleting by `.id` instead of object, leaving stale designations.
  - Fixed relax/wander task phase never advancing from `approach`.
  - `setPointerCapture` guarded with try/catch for synthetic/edge cases.
- Visual improvements:
  - Moved pond to `{ x: 14.5, z: 16, rx: 5.0, rz: 4.2, level: -0.32 }`, clearing the cabin.
  - Reduced dirt patch opacity/size, brightened grass palette, darkened/reduced grass tufts.
  - Added 8 close framing trees.
  - Increased exposure to `1.14`, hemi intensity to `1.04`, landscape camera distance to `28`.
  - Water now darkens at night via `uDay`.
  - Slightly stronger campfire smoke.
- Fixed initial clutter: selection panel starts hidden (`hidden` class in `index.html`).
- Verified:
  - Mobile screenshots 390×844, 360×640, landscape 844×390.
  - Desktop 1440×900.
  - Selection panel/portrait, build sheet, ghost placement, toasts, log/objectives, menu, help.
  - Build completion by colonists and objective completion.
  - Chop/mine designation and hauling.
  - Speed controls, pinch zoom, twist rotate, pinch-pan, one-finger pan.
  - Night, rain, sunset visuals.
  - Production build succeeds (`npx vite build`, 735 KB JS / 191 KB gzip).

### Active
- Investigating sleep/pathing bug: colonists can get stuck in sleep `approach` phase, notably Ivo with bed `b25`.
- Debug showed bed sleep spot is inside bed footprint (e.g. bed at `21,22`, spot `21,23` is blocked); `findPath` may pick an endpoint not satisfying `atSpot` (Ivo arrived at `23,24`, spot `21,23`, so `atSpot` false), leaving him stuck all night.
- Need to fix sleep destination selection so it targets a walkable adjacent tile and `atSpot` consistently succeeds.

### Blocked
- None.

## Next Move
1. Fix sleep destination: choose a walkable adjacent tile outside the bed footprint (or relax `atSpot` to handle path endpoint), ensuring bed sleepers reach `fallAsleep`.
2. Re-run `/tmp/opencode/sleep.mjs` and confirm all assigned bed occupants sleep, rest recovers, and night/day transitions work.
3. Re-run long simulation (`/tmp/opencode/simulate.mjs`) for stale errors and verify no stuck tasks.
4. Optionally improve near-label spacing and polish dusk lighting / rain transition.
5. Re-run production build and final mobile/desktop captures.
6. Consider committing the currently uncommitted work once stable.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/Yu/Yu/src/entities.js`: sleep/relax/wander task logic, monkey-patched `onReachTask`, `beginSleep`, work completion.
- `/home/runner/work/Yu/Yu/src/colony.js`: camp setup, beds, jobs, needs, objectives, resources, sleep/think logic.
- `/home/runner/work/Yu/Yu/src/pathfinding.js`: A* and `findNearestWalkable`, relevant to bed approach bug.
- `/home/runner/work/Yu/Yu/src/world.js`: terrain, pond, trees, grass, water shader, height sampling, wind, lighting.
- `/home/runner/work/Yu/Yu/src/input.js`: camera rig, touch gestures, placement input, pinch-pan.
- `/home/runner/work/Yu/Yu/src/main.js`: bootstrap, render loop, placement, rain, simulation API.
- `/home/runner/work/Yu/Yu/src/ui.js`: HUD, selection panel, portraits, labels, alerts, sheet behavior.
- `/home/runner/work/Yu/Yu/src/buildings.js`: building models and placement metadata.
- `/home/runner/work/Yu/Yu/src/style.css`: mobile/desktop HUD layout.
- `/home/runner/work/Yu/Yu/index.html`: HUD DOM, selection panel starts hidden.
- `/home/runner/work/Yu/Yu/screenshots/`: verification captures.
- `/tmp/opencode/sleep.mjs`: reproduction for overnight sleep behavior.
- `/tmp/opencode/capture.mjs`: Playwright screenshot/console harness.
- `/tmp/opencode/simulate.mjs`: long-run gameplay/error simulation.

## Important Context
- Dev server: `http://localhost:3002`; log `/tmp/ridgewood-dev.log`.
- Screenshot command: `node /tmp/opencode/capture.mjs <url> <output.png> <width> <height> <waitMs>`.
- Playwright requires headed browser with `DISPLAY` from `~/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/display`; helper handles this.
- Debug scripts: `/tmp/opencode/debug.mjs`, `debug-place2.mjs`, `debug-work.mjs`, `debug-sleep.mjs`, `work.mjs`, `touch.mjs`, `pinch.mjs`, `weather.mjs`, `ui-test.mjs`, `path.mjs`, `grid.mjs`.
- Sleep bug reproduction output:
  - Beds: `b25@21,22` footprint `21,22|21,23`, `b26@23,22` footprint `23,22|23,23`.
  - Bed spots used: `{tx: bed.tx, tz: bed.tz + 1}` → blocked.
  - Ivo path ended at `23,24`, `spotTiles {tx:21,tz:23}`, so `atSpot` false.
- `findPath` uses `findNearestWalkable` for blocked goals, but destination may not be within `atSpot` tolerance.
- All changes remain uncommitted in the repo.
- Default capture harness may click a visible button labeled exactly “Start”/“Play”; current UI uses “Got it”/“Next”, so no conflict.
